d.why: Principal Conway of Midtown Science only introduces valedictorian Gwen Stacy at the graduation in The Amazing Spider-Man 2, one short scene that changes nothing.
Jorge's mother only screams when her son slips through the police line during the Rhino standoff and hugs him when Spider-Man sends him back, with no real lines and no part in the plot.
Agent Berkley is one of the two FBI men who told Ben and May that Richard Parker was a traitor, but that visit is only told in May's own words and he has no lines of his own.
Rosie Collins is one of the Life Foundation lab scientists around Drake's symbiote trials, with only technical lab chatter and no action of her own that the story turns on.
Lloyd Emerson is one of the Life Foundation lab scientists around Drake's symbiote trials, with only technical lab chatter and no action of his own that the story turns on.
Corinne Wan is the Malaysian paramedic Riot jumps into at the crash site; what she does on screen afterwards is Riot's doing, covered by Riot's file, and she has no part of her own.
Ziggy is Eddie's hotel neighbor who agrees to turn his music down in one brief exchange that changes nothing.
Ziggy's girlfriend is only a background presence with her boyfriend, with no lines or part in the story.
Jacob is one of Drake's test subjects whom the blue symbiote kills from inside, with no lines and no part of his own in the plot.
Dr. Camille Pazzo is the Ravencroft doctor who taunts Frances over the speaker in the single scene where Carnage breaks in, a short scene her presence changes nothing in.
Kristen Simoes is a real San Francisco TV reporter appearing as herself in a news report, so she stays out.
M. Carroll is one of the San Quentin guards in the execution-chamber massacre with no lines or actions of his own that the story turns on.
N. Brown is one of the San Quentin guards in the execution-chamber massacre with no lines or actions of his own that the story turns on.
D. Lopez is one of the San Quentin guards seen at Kasady's execution and escape with no lines or actions of his own that the story turns on.
G. Murphy is one of the San Quentin guards Carnage kills in the execution-chamber massacre, one death among many with no part of his own.
Agony is the purple symbiote Teddy Paine bonds with at the end to save Sadie; it never speaks or acts for itself, so it is a creature with no character of its own.

Toxin is the green symbiote Imperium bonds to the dying Patrick Mulligan; it speaks in its own voice (Stephen Graham) when Teddy questions it, telling Imperium the symbiotes fled Knull and his creatures and warning of what is coming, then fights in the Area 51 battle.
Lasher is the green symbiote Sadie bonds with to fight the Xenophages; it never speaks or acts for itself, so it is a creature with no character of its own.
Captain Forrest is one of Strickland's Imperium soldiers in the raids on Eddie, with no lines or actions of his own that the story turns on.
Javier is the Mexican dogfighting thug who menaces Eddie in one short scene before Venom kills him and his men, a scene that changes nothing in the plot.

Thaddeus is Teddy Paine's twin brother, seen with her in flashbacks dreaming of space and NASA until lightning kills him; his death drives Teddy's work at Area 51, and she is called out for still living her brother's dream.
Animal is one of the Area 55 symbiotes released against the Xenophages that merges into Hybrid; it never speaks or acts for itself, so it is a creature with no character of its own.
Tendril is one of the Area 55 symbiotes released against the Xenophages that merges into Hybrid; it never speaks or acts for itself, so it is a creature with no character of its own.
Hybrid is the fused Animal-Tendril symbiote that fights in the Area 51 battle; it never speaks or acts for itself, so it is a creature with no character of its own.
Jade Clark is an Imperium lab technician who bonds with the White symbiote as one of several hosts in the final battle, with no lines or part of her own that the story turns on.
